title: DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The aggregate objective F may be nonconvex. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz for public L > 0, and it has a global lower bound a satisfying F(x₀) − a ≤ Δ for public Δ ≥ 0. Each worker objective is differentiable. The Lipschitz condition applies only to the aggregate gradient.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: F(x) = (1/n) ∑ᵢ fᵢ(x), with one local objective per worker and n ≥ 1.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Functions and objective. LongTails/Setups/DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params.n, Functions and objective. LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean, objective.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Worker i queries a point x and a positive batch size m. After m hᵢ time it receives m individual vectors gᵢ(x, ξ) from consecutive fresh samples of its mixture stream. The reply contains no indicator identifying clean samples.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.ComputeQuery, spec.ComputeReply and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, ComputeQuery, ComputeReply and computation.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x, the clean law μᵢ gives E[gᵢ(x, ξ)] = ∇fᵢ(x) and E‖gᵢ(x, ξ) − ∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ σᵢ². Each σᵢ ≥ 0 is public. These moment bounds apply to the clean component of each mixture.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient.unbiased and IsStochasticGradient.variance.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: Worker i draws IID samples from (1 − ηᵢ)μᵢ + ηᵢνᵢ, with independent streams across workers. The contaminating law νᵢ is arbitrary, so the observed gradient can be biased or lack a finite mean. The public rates satisfy 0 ≤ ηᵢ ≤ 1/16 and 2¹⁸ ∑ᵢ σᵢ√ηᵢ ≤ nε. The component functions, oracle maps and sampling laws are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params, mixture, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The decision space is ℝᵈ with the Euclidean norm. The dimension d and starting point x₀ are public.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Point and spec.publicInput. LongTails/Setups/DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params.d, Params.x0 and Point.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The budget measures elapsed time. Workers compute concurrently, with at most one pending batch per worker and public per-sample times hᵢ > 0. Every ordered worker pair has its own serial message queue, so distinct links can operate concurrently. A k-bit payload occupies its link for ℓ + b(k + 64), including the clock overhead, with public ℓ, b ≥ 0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex.lean, network, spec.publicInput and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, computation, Mail and communication. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, clockBits, step and TimedConvergence.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The designated root returns a single measurable point X at the prescribed deadline. The stationarity criterion is ‖∇F(X)‖ ≤ ε for the clean aggregate objective and public ε > 0.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.Output, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute and TimedConvergence.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: Pr(‖∇F(X)‖ > ε) ≤ failure, with public 0 < failure < 1. Probability is taken over the product of the algorithm seed law and the joint worker-sample law.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params.failure, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law and TimedConvergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines worker-specific sample contamination and aggregate-only smoothness with a high-probability stationarity target under a fixed elapsed-time budget. Both heterogeneous sampling times and concurrent, bit-priced communication enter that budget.

descriptionHtml:
Distributed Stationarity Under Gradient Contamination

We seek a stationary point of a possibly nonconvex objective F on Rd, where d is a nonnegative integer. The objective averages differentiable worker losses, has a Lipschitz gradient, and has a bounded initial gap above a global lower bound. Workers communicate over directed links and return batches of local gradient estimates from independent sample streams. Each stream consists of independent draws from a worker-specific mixture of a clean law yielding unbiased estimates with bounded variance and an arbitrary contaminating law. For tolerance ε>0 and failure probability δ∈(0,1), the goal is a measurable output x¯ with ∥∇F(x¯)∥≤ε with probability at least 1−δ by the allotted time.

For n≥1 workers with local losses fi:Rd→R, write F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x). The optimization problem is infx∈RdF(x). We use the Euclidean norm. The algorithm receives d, n, the measurable sample space Ω, the starting point x0∈Rd, the smoothness and gap bounds L and Δ, the worker noise and contamination bounds (σi,ηi)i=1n, the computation times (hi)i=1n, the link latency ℓ and per-bit time b, and the targets ε and δ.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Aggregate smoothness and initial gap). Each fi is differentiable everywhere. For some global lower bound a∈R, the constants L>0 and Δ≥0 satisfy ∥∇F(x)−∇F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥for all x,y∈Rd,a≤F(x)for all x∈Rd,F(x0)−a≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Clean local gradients). Worker i has a jointly measurable map gi:Rd×Ω→Rd and a clean probability law μi on Ω. For each x∈Rd and Z∼μi, the vector gi(x,Z) is Bochner integrable, its squared error is integrable, and, with σi≥0, EZ∼μi[gi(x,Z)]=∇fi(x),EZ∼μi[∥gi(x,Z)−∇fi(x)∥2]≤σi2.

Assumption 3 (Contaminated sampling). The sample streams (Zi,k)k≥0 are independent across workers and independent of the algorithm’s randomness. Within stream i, the samples are measurable and i.i.d. with law (1−ηi)μi+ηiνi, where νi is an arbitrary probability law on Ω. The contamination fractions and target tolerance satisfy 0≤ηi≤116(1≤i≤n),218∑i=1nσiηi≤nε.

A computation query at worker i specifies a point x∈Rd and a positive integer batch size m. If k samples have already been used, the reply is the ordered list (gi(x,Zi,k+j))j=0m−1, available after mhi units of time, where hi>0. Each worker handles one batch at a time and ignores further computation requests while a batch is pending. Different workers can compute concurrently.

Every ordered pair of workers, including a worker paired with itself, has a directed link. A message with a payload of q≥0 bits is padded with 64 zero bits and occupies its link for ℓ+b(q+64) units of time, where ℓ,b≥0. The recipient receives the sender’s identity and the padded bit string. Messages on each link are served in submission order. Distinct links can transmit concurrently, and communication can overlap computation.

For an elapsed-time budget T≥0, almost surely only finitely many events may occur at every deadline up to and including T. The designated root worker’s output x¯∈Rd at time T must be measurable and satisfy P(∥∇F(x¯)∥>ε)≤δ, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the worker sample streams.

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, F=n−1∑ifi averages differentiable local objectives, has L-Lipschitz gradient and initial gap at most Δ. Honest workers sample independently across workers and IID locally from (1−ηi)μi+ηiνi, with arbitrary νi and 0≤ηi≤1/16. Under μi the jointly measurable gradient oracle is unbiased for ∇fi with variance at most σi2. All setup parameters are public. Each worker has one batch in flight and pays hi>0 per sample. The complete directed network allows concurrent links and serializes messages per link, with cost ℓ+bm for m bits. The target is one measurable X with Pr(∥∇F(X)∥>ε)≤δ, where 0<δ<1, ε>0 and ε≥218n−1∑iσiηi.

Stationarity under distributed Huber contamination
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ContaminatedParallelStationarity (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) Elapsed-time upper bound O((K+qmin{K,q})(H+S)+K[(1+log⁡n)H+C])
(2) FiniteBitLeon (Tyurin 2026a) Time O(K(H+S+C)) for E∥∇F(X)∥2≤ε2. (1) handles Huber contamination and heterogeneous variances. On the clean common-variance restriction, gives high probability at the same time order for q≤K and fixed n. (1) adds KHlog⁡n pilot time on the clean overlap and gives no expected squared-norm guarantee.
(3) Leon SGD (Tyurin 2026b, Thm. 1.7) Time O(Kmax{d/w¯,H,S}) for E∥∇F(X)∥2≤ε2. (1) handles contamination and heterogeneous variances with tunable high probability. (3) needs clean samples with a common variance bound. Time bounds are incomparable across network models. (1) requires a complete network. (3) uses a bandwidth graph.
(4) Derived bound, robust minibatch descent O(K[1+(σ12/ε2)log⁡(K/δ)]) samples, n=1. Union bound with robust mean error O(σ1η1+σ1log⁡(K/δ)/N) above a sufficient contamination floor. (1) uses O(K(1+σ12/ε2)) samples for q≤K, removing log⁡(K/δ) from the noise term. The total improves when that term dominates.
(5) Derived bound, retuned NSGD (Hübler et al. 2025, Thm. 4) O(Kq(1+σ12/ε2)) samples, clean n=1, for high-probability average gradient norm ≤ε. (1) uses O(K(1+σ12/ε2)) samples for q≤K and returns a certified point. (5) needs bounded conditional mean estimation error, which contamination can invalidate. (1) gives no trajectory-average guarantee.

import LongTails.Setups.DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex
import LongTails.Setups.BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex

open MeasureTheory DistributedTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex

open StochasticSmoothAndConvex (IsStochasticGradient)
open StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex (IID)

structure Params extends DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.Params where
  η : Fin n → ℝ
  failure : ℝ

abbrev Point (p : Params) := DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.Point p.toParams
abbrev Functions (p : Params) := DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.Functions p.toParams
abbrev Samples (p : Params) := DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.Samples p.toParams
noncomputable abbrev objective (p : Params) := DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.objective p.toParams

noncomputable abbrev network (p : Params) : DistributedSmoothNonconvex.Params :=
  { d := p.d, n := p.n, Ω := p.Ω, h := p.h, l := p.l, b := p.b, L := p.L,
    Δ := p.Δ, ε := p.ε, σ := ⨆ i, p.σ i, x0 := p.x0 }

noncomputable def mixture {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (η : ℝ)
    (μ ν : Measure Ω) : Measure Ω :=
  ENNReal.ofReal (1 - η) • μ + ENNReal.ofReal η • ν

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  numWorkers p := p.n
  Instance := Functions
  ComputeQuery p := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.ComputeQuery (network p)
  ComputeReply p := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.ComputeReply (network p)
  CommReply p := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.CommReply (network p)
  Output := Point
  publicInput := id
  valid p := (∀ i, 0 < p.h i) ∧ 0 < p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧
    (∀ i, 0 ≤ p.σ i ∧ 0 ≤ p.η i ∧ p.η i ≤ 1 / 16) ∧ 0 < p.failure ∧ p.failure < 1 ∧
    2 ^ 18 * (∑ i, p.σ i * Real.sqrt (p.η i)) ≤ (p.n : ℝ) * p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ i x, HasGradientAt (f i) (gradient (f i) x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient (objective p f) x - gradient (objective p f) y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ lower : ℝ, (∀ x, lower ≤ objective p f x) ∧ objective p f p.x0 - lower ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ∃ (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p)
      (μ ν : Fin p.n → ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)),
      O = BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.system (network p) g P ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i (s : Samples p) => s i) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∀ i, IID (fun k (s : Samples p) => s i k) (mixture (p.η i) (μ i) (ν i)) (P : Measure _) ∧
        IsStochasticGradient (Point p) p.Ω (μ i) (f i) (g i) (p.σ i)
  successful p f X P :=
    Measurable X ∧ (P : Measure _) {s | p.ε < ‖gradient (objective p f) (X s)‖} ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal p.failure

end LongTails.Setups.DistributedContaminatedSmoothNonconvex
